grid.title: Grid: clean lines
steps: Keep your whole spin in frame. Use Fit center & size to center the grid around your visible staves.
White lines are the paths. Green tip rings mean you are within tolerance; orange arrows point toward the nearest line.
Size changes the grid width. Match staff length makes its width equal to a staff; then adjust Size for your intended pattern. Center X/Y moves it, and Rotation tilts it.
For an off-angle camera, mark a real rectangle in your movement plane with Calibrate viewing angle. Keep the camera fixed. Beat points mark the grid perimeter when timing is enabled.

circles.title: Circles: steady radii
steps: Use Fit center & size while holding the staves in your normal spinning positions. It estimates the center, circle radius, and circle separation.
Match staff length sets the circle diameter to your staff length. Adjust Separation to place each circle around its spin center. Single-staff mode uses one circle.
Trace the white circumferences. Green rings indicate radial alignment; orange arrows show which way the tips need to move.
Enable beat practice and pass the numbered points on the pulse. Timing in milliseconds and position error in percent are independent. The small filled tip is the timing tip.

cube.title: Cube: align with vertices
steps: The cube is a projected guide in front of you. Fit center & size, then adjust Size and Projection depth to place its corners where you intend to reach.
Aim the staff tips at the white corner points. Orange arrows lead to the nearest vertex; green rings show a tip within tolerance.
Calibrate viewing angle with a real rectangle in your movement plane if the camera is off to one side. It corrects that plane, not movement toward or away from the camera.
The camera does not recover 3D depth. Use cube error for chosen alignment moments, not as a grade for every transition between corners.

free.title: Free flow: watch your paths
steps: Keep the full movement in view. Startup fitting begins at the widest camera angle and adjusts conservatively once tracking is reliable.
Brighter lime and purple trails show the last 4.2 seconds. Turn Tip trails off to simplify the view. Briefly hidden tips keep their identity while precise scores pause.
There is no grid-alignment score here. Choose one double-ended staff or two, and record a session to inspect your paths afterward.
For rhythmic spins, enable beat practice. The numbered circle points give timing and position feedback even in Free flow. Adjust center and size to your spin.
